proof_summary: Split the summation into indices divisible and not divisible by \(p\), and factor each binomial coefficient into a lower-level binomial coefficient times the prime-to-\(p\) product \(\prod_{p\nmid i}(1+N/i)\). Wolstenholme-type bounds for reciprocal residue sums make a second-order expansion of this product control the divisible indices, while blockwise descent of inverse-square auxiliary sums controls the nondivisible indices; together these give order \(p^{3r}\), with the general case obtained by extracting the \(p\)-power from \(n\).
